questions.prompt_text: In astable multivibrator if charging time constant is equal to discharging time constant, duty cycle is ______.
questions.prompt_html: In astable multivibrator if charging time constant is equal to discharging time constant, duty cycle is ______.
questions.solution_html:
Correct Answer: (i) 50%

If charging time constant τc = discharging time constant τd, then TON = TOFF. Duty cycle D = TON / (TON + TOFF) = 1/2 = 50% (symmetrical square wave).

questions.prompt_text: ______ stage of operational amplifier rejects the noise.
questions.prompt_html: ______ stage of operational amplifier rejects the noise.
questions.solution_html:
Correct Answer: (ii) Differential Amplifier

The input stage of an op-amp is a differential amplifier. Noise picked up equally on both inputs acts as a common-mode signal Vn and cancels in the difference V1 − V2 (high CMRR).

Correct Answer: (i) Temperature Transducer

At constant forward current, a silicon PN junction diode's forward voltage drop VF varies linearly with temperature (approx. −2 mV/°C), making it useful as a temperature transducer.

questions.prompt_text: A Zener voltage regulator is to be designed for output of 10 volts. If the input voltage to the regulator is 25 volts, find the value of current limiting resistor. Given Pz = 500 mW.
questions.prompt_html: A Zener voltage regulator is to be designed for output of 10 volts. If the input voltage to the regulator is 25 volts, find the value of current limiting resistor. Given Pz = 500 mW.
questions.solution_html:
Given: Vz = 10 V, Vin = 25 V, Pz = 500 mW = 0.5 W

  • Maximum Zener current: Iz(max) = Pz / Vz = 0.5 / 10 = 0.05 A (50 mA)
  • Voltage drop across series resistor Rs: VR = Vin − Vz = 25 − 10 = 15 V
  • Current limiting resistor: Rs = (Vin − Vz) / Iz(max) = 15 / 0.05 = 300 Ω

questions.prompt_text: What are the drawbacks of RC coupled amplifier?
questions.prompt_html: What are the drawbacks of RC coupled amplifier?
questions.solution_html:
1. Cannot amplify DC / very low frequencies: Coupling capacitor blocks DC (XC = 1/(2πfC) becomes very high at low frequency), causing gain drop.
  2. Poor high-frequency response: Transistor junction and stray capacitances bypass high-frequency signals to ground.
  3. No impedance matching: Output impedance is high compared to load impedance, giving poor power transfer efficiency.
  4. Low voltage & power gain compared to transformer-coupled amplifiers at narrow bands, plus stage interaction/loading effects.

questions.prompt_text: Explain the use of Cathode Ray Oscilloscope for measurement of AC and DC voltage.
questions.prompt_html: Explain the use of Cathode Ray Oscilloscope for measurement of AC and DC voltage.
questions.solution_html:
1. DC Voltage Measurement:

  • Set input coupling to GND and center the horizontal trace at 0 reference line.
  • Switch coupling to DC and apply the unknown DC voltage to Y-input.
  • Measure vertical shift d in divisions: VDC = d × (VOLTS/DIV).

2. AC Voltage Measurement:

  • Set coupling to AC and apply the AC signal to vertical input; adjust TIME/DIV and VOLTS/DIV.
  • Measure total peak-to-peak vertical height h in divisions.
  • Vp-p = h × (VOLTS/DIV); Vp = Vp-p / 2; for sine wave Vrms = Vp / √2.

questions.prompt_text: What do you mean by Network Topology? Enlist the types of network topologies and explain any one of them with diagram.
questions.prompt_html: What do you mean by Network Topology? Enlist the types of network topologies and explain any one of them with diagram.
questions.solution_html:
Definition: Network topology is the physical or logical layout/arrangement in which computers (nodes) and links are interconnected in a computer network.

Types (syllabus): Star topology, Ring topology, Bus topology (also Mesh, Tree, Hybrid).

Star Topology: Every workstation/node connects via a dedicated point-to-point cable to a central hub/switch. All communication passes through the central hub. Failure of one cable/node does not affect others, though hub failure brings down the network.

questions.prompt_text: Write a note on LDR.
questions.prompt_html: Write a note on LDR.
questions.solution_html:
LDR (Light Dependent Resistor / Photoresistor): A passive transducer whose electrical resistance varies inversely with incident light intensity.

  • Principle & Construction: Works on photoconductivity using a zigzag track of semiconductor such as Cadmium Sulphide (CdS) on a ceramic base.
  • Working: In darkness, few free charge carriers exist, so resistance is very high (~MΩ). When light photons strike the CdS surface, electron-hole pairs are generated and resistance drops sharply (to a few hundred Ω).
  • Applications: Automatic street light switches, twilight relays, camera exposure meters, optical burglar alarms.

questions.prompt_text: In a circuit of Schmitt trigger R1 = 10 kOhm, R2 = 2 kOhm, Vin = 3 Vp-p sinewave, with saturation voltage of +-13 volts. Calculate: (i) UTP, (ii) LTP, (iii) Hysteresis voltage, (iv) Feedback factor beta.
questions.prompt_html:
In a circuit of Schmitt trigger R1 = 10 kΩ, R2 = 2 kΩ, Vin = 3 Vp-p sinewave, with saturation voltage of ±13 volts. Calculate:

(i) UTP   (ii) LTP   (iii) Hysteresis voltage   (iv) Feedback factor β
questions.solution_html:
Given: R1 = 10 kΩ, R2 = 2 kΩ, Vsat = ±13 V.

  1. (iv) Feedback factor β: β = R2 / (R1 + R2) = 2 / (10 + 2) = 2/12 = 0.1667
  2. (i) Upper Trigger Point (UTP): UTP = +β Vsat = (1/6) × 13 = +2.167 V
  3. (ii) Lower Trigger Point (LTP): LTP = −β Vsat = −(1/6) × 13 = −2.167 V
  4. (iii) Hysteresis voltage (VH): VH = UTP − LTP = 2.167 − (−2.167) = 4.333 V

Note: Since Vin = 3 Vp-p (±1.5 V peak) < UTP (2.167 V), output stays latched without switching unless Vin crosses ±2.167 V.

questions.prompt_text: State eight advantages of fibre optic cable over conventional electrical cable for communication.
questions.prompt_html: State eight advantages of fibre optic cable over conventional electrical cable for communication.
questions.solution_html:
1. Extremely wide bandwidth: Carries vastly higher data rates/channels.
  2. Low attenuation: Signals travel much farther without repeaters.
  3. Immunity to EMI & RFI: Glass/plastic fibers are dielectric and unaffected by electromagnetic noise.
  4. No crosstalk: Light stays confined inside the core via total internal reflection.
  5. High security: Very difficult to tap without detection.
  6. Electrical safety & isolation: No spark hazard or ground loops in explosive environments.
  7. Smaller size & lighter weight: Thinner and much lighter than copper bundles.
  8. Corrosion resistance & longer life: Silica glass does not corrode like copper.

questions.prompt_text: The turns ratio of transformer in a bridge rectifier is 12:1. Primary is connected to 230 volts, 50 Hz AC mains. Find the output of DC voltage under no load condition, assume the voltage drop across each diode to be zero.
questions.prompt_html: The turns ratio of transformer in a bridge rectifier is 12:1. Primary is connected to 230 volts, 50 Hz AC mains. Find the output of DC voltage under no load condition, assume the voltage drop across each diode to be zero.
questions.solution_html:
Given: Vp = 230 V, Np : Ns = 12 : 1, Vd = 0 V.

  • Secondary RMS voltage: Vs(rms) = 230 / 12 = 19.17 V
  • Peak secondary voltage: Vm = Vs(rms) × √2 = 19.167 × 1.414 = 27.11 V
  • Average (DC) output voltage (full-wave bridge): Vdc = 2Vm / π = (2 × 27.11) / 3.1416 = 17.26 V

questions.prompt_html: The deflection sensitivity of CRT is 0.04 mm/V. An unknown voltage applied to X-plates causes the deflection of spot 5 mm horizontally. Find the value of unknown voltage.
questions.solution_html:

questions.prompt_text: Explain the working of Piezoelectric Transducer.
questions.prompt_html: Explain the working of Piezoelectric Transducer.
questions.solution_html:
Active Transducer (Piezoelectric Effect):

  • Uses crystals like quartz, Rochelle salt, or barium titanate placed between two metal electrodes.
  • When mechanical force/pressure deforms the crystal, internal electric dipoles align and produce a measurable potential difference across the electrodes without any external power supply.
  • Induced charge Q = d × F, where d is charge sensitivity and F is applied force.
  • Uses: Dynamic pressure sensors, accelerometers, ultrasonic generators, pickups. (Cannot measure static DC pressure because charge leaks away.)

questions.prompt_text: List any four advantages of SMPS.
questions.prompt_html: List any four advantages of SMPS.
questions.solution_html:
1. High efficiency (75%–90%): Pass transistor operates only in saturation or cut-off, minimizing I²R heat dissipation compared to linear regulators.
  2. Compact & lightweight: High-frequency switching (20 kHz+) permits tiny ferrite-core transformers and small filter capacitors.
  3. Wide input voltage tolerance: Regulates steady DC output over large AC mains fluctuations.
  4. Low heat generation: Needs smaller heat sinks and supports multiple isolated output voltages from one transformer.

questions.prompt_text: Draw the circuit diagram of Inverting Operational Amplifier and obtain an expression for its gain. Explain how it can be used as sign changer.
questions.prompt_html: Draw the circuit diagram of Inverting Operational Amplifier and obtain an expression for its gain. Explain how it can be used as sign changer.
questions.solution_html:
Circuit: Input Vin connects via resistor R1 to the inverting (−) pin; feedback resistor Rf connects output Vout back to (−); non-inverting (+) pin is grounded (0 V).

Derivation:

  1. By virtual ground, V− = V+ = 0 V, and op-amp draws negligible input current (IB ≈ 0).
  2. Input current I1 = (Vin − 0)/R1 equals feedback current If = (0 − Vout)/Rf.
  3. Vin/R1 = −Vout/Rf ⇒ Av = Vout / Vin = −Rf / R1.

Sign Changer (Unity Gain Inverter): Set Rf = R1, giving Av = −1 and Vout = −Vin (180° phase / polarity reversal).

questions.prompt_text: Explain the working of IC 555 as a Monostable Multivibrator.
questions.prompt_html: Explain the working of IC 555 as a Monostable Multivibrator.
questions.solution_html:
A monostable (one-shot) multivibrator has one stable state (output LOW) and one quasi-stable state (output HIGH) of duration T = 1.1 R C.

  1. Initial stable state: Flip-flop Q̅ = 1 keeps discharge transistor Q1 ON, holding capacitor C shorted to 0 V; output (pin 3) is LOW.
  2. Triggering: Applying a negative pulse (< 1/3 VCC) at pin 2 makes lower comparator SET the flip-flop (Q̅ = 0), turning Q1 OFF and making output HIGH.
  3. Timing & Reset: C charges through R toward VCC. When VC reaches 2/3 VCC, upper comparator RESETS the flip-flop, turning Q1 ON to discharge C rapidly and returning output to LOW.

questions.prompt_text: Explain how CRO displays a waveform.
questions.prompt_html: Explain how CRO displays a waveform.
questions.solution_html:
1. Vertical deflection (Y-axis): The unknown input signal passes through the vertical amplifier & delay line to the vertical deflection plates, moving the electron beam vertically proportional to instantaneous voltage V(t).
  2. Horizontal deflection (X-axis): A sawtooth sweep voltage from the time-base generator is applied to the horizontal deflection plates, sweeping the spot linearly from left to right with time and flying back rapidly during retrace (blanked).
  3. Synchronization (Trigger): The trigger circuit starts each horizontal sweep at the same phase point of the input waveform, producing a stationary trace V(t) on the phosphor screen due to persistence of vision.

questions.prompt_text: State any eight characteristics of ideal Op-Amplifier.
questions.prompt_html: State any eight characteristics of ideal Op-Amplifier.
questions.solution_html:
1. Infinite open-loop voltage gain (AOL = ∞)
  2. Infinite input impedance (Rin = ∞, draws zero input current)
  3. Zero output impedance (Rout = 0, drives any load without drop)
  4. Infinite bandwidth (BW = ∞, flat response from DC upward)
  5. Infinite CMRR (CMRR = ∞, rejects all common-mode noise)
  6. Infinite slew rate (SR = ∞, output changes instantaneously)
  7. Zero input offset voltage (Vos = 0 when V1 = V2)
  8. Zero thermal drift (characteristics unaffected by temperature)

questions.prompt_text: Draw internal block diagram of IC555 and explain its working.
questions.prompt_html: Draw internal block diagram of IC555 and explain its working.
questions.solution_html:
Internal Blocks of IC 555:

  1. Potential Divider: Three matched 5 kΩ resistors between VCC and GND fix upper reference = 2/3 VCC and lower reference = 1/3 VCC.
  2. Upper Comparator (Threshold): Compares pin 6 with 2/3 VCC; goes HIGH to RESET the flip-flop when V6 > 2/3 VCC.
  3. Lower Comparator (Trigger): Compares pin 2 with 1/3 VCC; goes HIGH to SET the flip-flop when V2 < 1/3 VCC.
  4. SR Flip-Flop & Output Stage: Complementary output Q̅ drives the inverting output buffer (pin 3, sinks/sources up to 200 mA). Pin 4 resets directly.
  5. Discharge Transistor (Q1): Driven by Q̅; turns ON to discharge timing capacitor via pin 7 when output is LOW.

questions.prompt_text: Define deflection sensitivity of CRO. What is the function of delay line in CRO?
questions.prompt_html: Define deflection sensitivity of CRO. What is the function of delay line in CRO?
questions.solution_html:
Deflection Sensitivity (S): Vertical (or horizontal) displacement D of the electron beam spot on the CRT screen per unit voltage V applied to the deflection plates: S = D / V (unit: mm/V).

Function of Delay Line: Inserted in the vertical amplifier path (approx. 150–200 ns delay) so the vertical signal reaches the deflection plates slightly after the trigger circuit initiates the horizontal sweep—preventing loss of the leading edge of fast pulses.

questions.prompt_text: A single phase half wave rectifier supplies power to 1 kOhm load. The input supply voltage is 220 VRMS. Neglect the forward resistance of diode. Calculate average voltage and current in the circuit.
questions.prompt_html: A single phase half wave rectifier supplies power to 1 kΩ load. The input supply voltage is 220 VRMS. Neglect the forward resistance of diode. Calculate average voltage and current in the circuit.
questions.solution_html:
Given: Vrms = 220 V, RL = 1 kΩ = 1000 Ω.

  • Peak voltage: Vm = √2 × 220 = 311.13 V
  • Average (DC) output voltage: Vdc = Vm / π = 311.13 / 3.1416 = 99.04 V (or 0.45 × 220 = 99 V)
  • Average load current: Idc = Vdc / RL = 99.04 / 1000 = 99.04 mA

questions.prompt_text: Explain the working of Loudspeaker with neat diagram.
questions.prompt_html: Explain the working of Loudspeaker with neat diagram.
questions.solution_html:
Dynamic Moving-Coil Loudspeaker: An output electro-acoustic transducer that converts audio electrical current into sound pressure waves.

  • Construction: Permanent pot magnet producing radial magnetic field, lightweight cylindrical voice coil attached to a conical paper/plastic diaphragm (cone) suspended by a spider/surround.
  • Working: Varying AF current in the voice coil creates an alternating magnetic field that interacts with the permanent magnet field (F = BIl). The cone vibrates back and forth at the audio frequency, pushing air to produce sound waves.

questions.prompt_text: What is cell in cellular phone system? Explain in brief.
questions.prompt_html: What is cell in cellular phone system? Explain in brief.
questions.solution_html:
• A cell is a small subdivided geographic region covered by one low-power base station (BS) antenna/transceiver in a mobile cellular network.
  • Dividing a large city into many cells (modeled as non-overlapping hexagons) allows limited radio channels to be reused in non-adjacent cells without co-channel interference, dramatically multiplying subscriber capacity.
  • All cells connect to a central MTSO (Mobile Telephone Switching Office) which performs automatic handoff as a user moves between cells.

questions.prompt_text: State any three advantages of Op-Amp over normal amplifier.
questions.prompt_html: State any three advantages of Op-Amp over normal amplifier.
questions.solution_html:
1. Stable, predictable closed-loop gain: External resistor ratio sets exact gain independent of transistor beta/temperature variations.
  2. Versatility & Compact IC form: One tiny 8-pin IC (e.g. IC 741) performs amplification, addition, integration, differentiation, comparison, or filtering.
  3. Very high input impedance & low output impedance + DC amplification: Negligible source loading and direct-coupled internal stages amplify down to 0 Hz (DC).

questions.prompt_html: State any two Linear and Non-linear applications of Op-Amp.
questions.solution_html:

questions.prompt_text: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of following types of filter circuits: (i) Capacitor input filter (ii) Inductor filter (iii) R.C. filter (iv) L.C. filter
questions.prompt_html: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of following types of filter circuits: (i) Capacitor input filter (ii) Inductor filter (iii) R.C. filter (iv) L.C. filter
questions.solution_html:
• (i) Capacitor input filter: Adv: High DC output voltage (nearly Vm), low cost. Disadv: High surge current through diodes; poor regulation at heavy loads.
  • (ii) Inductor (Choke) filter: Adv: Ripple decreases as load current increases (good for heavy loads). Disadv: Lower DC output voltage; bulky/expensive iron-core inductor.
  • (iii) R.C. filter: Adv: Cheap, compact, lightweight (no bulky choke). Disadv: Poor voltage regulation & I²R power loss in series resistor R.
  • (iv) L.C. (L-section) filter: Adv: Very low ripple factor and relatively load-independent ripple. Disadv: Bulky and costly due to both inductor L and large capacitor C.

questions.prompt_text: Explain the working of centre-tap full wave rectifier with neat diagram and wave-form.
questions.prompt_html: Explain the working of centre-tap full wave rectifier with neat diagram and wave-form.
questions.solution_html:
Contains a center-tapped step-down transformer, 2 diodes D1, D2, and load resistor RL connected from common cathodes to the center tap.

  • Positive half-cycle: End A is +ve wrt center tap → D1 forward biased (conducts), D2 reverse biased. Current flows through RL top-to-bottom.
  • Negative half-cycle: End B becomes +ve wrt center tap → D2 forward biased (conducts), D1 OFF. Current again flows through RL top-to-bottom, yielding unidirectional pulsating DC on both half cycles (fripple = 2fin, Vdc = 2Vm/π).

questions.prompt_text: Explain the following parameters of an operational amplifier: (i) Input bias current (ii) CMRR (iii) Drift
questions.prompt_html: Explain the following parameters of an operational amplifier: (i) Input bias current (ii) CMRR (iii) Drift
questions.solution_html:
1. Input Bias Current (IB): Average of the two DC base currents flowing into the inverting and non-inverting input terminals: IB = (IB+ + IB−)/2. Ideal = 0.
  2. CMRR (Common Mode Rejection Ratio): Ratio of differential voltage gain Ad to common-mode voltage gain Acm: CMRR = |Ad / Acm| (or 20 log10|Ad/Acm| dB). Measures noise-rejection ability.
  3. Thermal Drift: Gradual change in input offset voltage (ΔVio/ΔT) or offset current (ΔIio/ΔT) per °C rise in ambient temperature/time.

questions.prompt_text: Calculate the output pulse width for the timer used as monostable multivibrator. Given, R = 15 kOhm and C = 0.22 uF. Find the value of C if pulse width changes to 20 ms.
questions.prompt_html: Calculate the output pulse width for the timer used as monostable multivibrator. Given, R = 15 kΩ and C = 0.22 μF. Find the value of C if pulse width changes to 20 ms.
questions.solution_html:
Formula (IC 555 Monostable): T = 1.1 × R × C

  1. For R = 15 × 103 Ω, C = 0.22 × 10−6 F:
    T = 1.1 × 15000 × 0.22 × 10−6 = 0.00363 s = 3.63 ms
  2. For T' = 20 ms = 20 × 10−3 s (with same R = 15 kΩ):
    C' = T' / (1.1 × R) = 0.02 / (1.1 × 15000) = 1.212 μF

questions.prompt_text: Draw labelled diagram of Cathode Ray Tube (CRT) and explain each electrode in it.
questions.prompt_html: Draw labelled diagram of Cathode Ray Tube (CRT) and explain each electrode in it.
questions.solution_html:
Main sections of CRT:

  • Electron Gun: Heater + indirectly heated barium-oxide cathode emits electrons; Control Grid (negative bias) controls beam intensity/brightness; Pre-accelerating anode accelerates beam; Focusing anode (variable +ve voltage) focuses electrons to a sharp spot; Accelerating anode gives final high velocity.
  • Deflection System: Vertical (Y) and Horizontal (X) electrostatic plates deflect beam according to applied voltages.
  • Fluorescent Screen & Aquadag: Inner phosphor screen converts kinetic energy to visible trace; conductive Aquadag collects secondary electrons.

questions.prompt_text: Explain with the help of circuit diagram, working of Inductor input filter, when it is connected across the output terminals of a full-wave rectifier. Draw its output wave-form.
questions.prompt_html: Explain with the help of circuit diagram, working of Inductor input filter, when it is connected across the output terminals of a full-wave rectifier. Draw its output wave-form.
questions.solution_html:
A high-value choke inductor L is connected in series between the full-wave rectifier output and load RL.

  • Working: An inductor offers very low DC resistance (so DC passes freely with minimal drop), while presenting high inductive reactance XL = 2πfL to AC ripple (f = 100 Hz). It also opposes sudden current changes via back-EMF (L di/dt), storing magnetic energy during peaks and releasing it during troughs.
  • Ripple Factor: γ = RL / (3√2 ωL) — decreases for heavier loads (smaller RL).

questions.prompt_text: Draw block diagram IC 555. Explain function of each block.
questions.prompt_html: Draw block diagram IC 555. Explain function of each block.
questions.solution_html:
1. Three 5 kΩ Resistors: Form a precision voltage divider providing 2/3 VCC and 1/3 VCC references.
  2. Upper & Lower Comparators: Monitor Threshold (pin 6 > 2/3 VCC resets) and Trigger (pin 2 < 1/3 VCC sets).
  3. SR Flip-Flop: Stores binary timer state; Pin 4 Reset overrides inputs immediately.
  4. Output Buffer (Pin 3): Inverts flip-flop Q̅ and delivers up to 200 mA load current.
  5. Discharge Transistor: Grounds Pin 7 during LOW output to discharge external C.

questions.prompt_text: Draw a circuit diagram of an Inverting amplifier using Op-amplifier. Explain concept of virtual ground and hence derive the expression for its output voltage.
questions.prompt_html: Draw a circuit diagram of an Inverting amplifier using Op-amplifier. Explain concept of virtual ground and hence derive the expression for its output voltage.
questions.solution_html:
Virtual Ground: Because open-loop gain AOL → ∞, differential input voltage Vd = Vout/AOL ≈ 0. With the (+) terminal grounded (0 V), the (−) terminal automatically sits at 0 V potential without being physically shorted to ground—called virtual ground.

Derivation:

  • Input current Iin = (Vin − 0)/R1
  • Op-amp draws zero current (Rin = ∞), so all Iin flows through Rf: If = (0 − Vout)/Rf
  • Equating Iin = If ⇒ Vout = −(Rf / R1) Vin

questions.prompt_text: What is Amplitude Modulation? State the expression for modulated wave and draw the waveform of modulated wave.
questions.prompt_html: What is Amplitude Modulation? State the expression for modulated wave and draw the waveform of modulated wave.
questions.solution_html:
Definition: Amplitude Modulation (AM) is the process in which the instantaneous amplitude of a high-frequency carrier wave varies linearly in accordance with the instantaneous amplitude of the modulating audio/baseband signal, keeping carrier frequency and phase constant.

Expression: vAM(t) = Vc(1 + m sin ωmt) sin ωct = Vc sin ωct + (mVc/2) cos(ωc − ωm)t − (mVc/2) cos(ωc + ωm)t, where modulation index m = Vm/Vc.

Waveform: High-frequency carrier whose upper and lower envelopes follow the low-frequency modulating sine wave between Vc(1+m) and Vc(1−m).

questions.prompt_text: With the help of Block diagram, explain the working of function Generator.
questions.prompt_html: With the help of Block diagram, explain the working of function Generator.
questions.solution_html:
A function generator produces standard sine, square, and triangular waveforms from ~0.01 Hz to several MHz.

  1. Frequency Controlled Network & Constant Current Sources: Upper current source charges timing capacitor C linearly upward; lower current source discharges it linearly downward.
  2. Integrator: Produces a linear triangular ramp wave as C charges/discharges between fixed upper/lower voltage thresholds.
  3. Voltage Comparator / Hysteresis Switch: Toggles sharply when triangle peaks hit threshold, driving the current switches and producing the Square Wave output.
  4. Resistance-Diode Sine Shaper: Shapes the triangular wave into a smooth low-distortion Sine Wave; output amplifiers/attenuators set amplitude and DC offset.

questions.prompt_text: Draw the circuit diagram of a voltage regulator using Zener diode, explain its working.
questions.prompt_html: Draw the circuit diagram of a voltage regulator using Zener diode, explain its working.
questions.solution_html:
Consists of a series current-limiting resistor Rs followed by a reverse-biased Zener diode connected in parallel (shunt) across load RL.

  • Input Variation (Line Regulation): If Vin increases, excess current flows through the low-resistance Zener breakdown path, increasing drop across Rs while Vout stays fixed at VZ.
  • Load Variation (Load Regulation): If IL increases, Zener current IZ decreases equally so total Is = IZ + IL remains constant, holding IsRs and thus Vout = VZ steady.

questions.prompt_text: In an Op-Amp Inverting adder, V1 = 0.2 volt, V2 = 0.1 volt, V3 = 0.4 volt, R1 = 1 kOhm, R2 = 2 kOhm, R3 = 4 kOhm. Find the output voltage if feed back resistance is 20 kOhm.
questions.prompt_html: In an Op-Amp Inverting adder, V1 = 0.2 V, V2 = 0.1 V, V3 = 0.4 V, R1 = 1 kΩ, R2 = 2 kΩ, R3 = 4 kΩ. Find the output voltage if feedback resistance is 20 kΩ.
questions.solution_html:
Formula (Weighted Inverting Summer):

Vout = −Rf [ (V1/R1) + (V2/R2) + (V3/R3) ]

  • V1/R1 = 0.2 / 1k = 0.2 mA
  • V2/R2 = 0.1 / 2k = 0.05 mA
  • V3/R3 = 0.4 / 4k = 0.1 mA
  • Total input current = 0.2 + 0.05 + 0.1 = 0.35 mA
  • Vout = −20 kΩ × 0.35 mA = −7.0 V

questions.prompt_text: Explain the working of LVDT as a transducer. Draw neat diagram. State its two applications.
questions.prompt_html: Explain the working of LVDT as a transducer. Draw neat diagram. State its two applications.
questions.solution_html:
LVDT (Linear Variable Differential Transformer): A passive inductive displacement transducer with one central primary coil (P) excited by AC and two identical series-opposing secondary coils (S1, S2) wound around a movable soft-iron core.

  • Working: Vout = ES1 − ES2. At the central null position, equal flux links both secondaries so Vout = 0. Moving the core left increases ES1 (Vout in phase); moving right increases ES2 (Vout 180° out of phase), linearly proportional to displacement.
  • Applications: Measurement of linear displacement/thickness, pressure (with diaphragm/Bourdon tube), and force/weight cells.

questions.prompt_text: What do you mean by Network Topology? Explain Star, Ring and Bus Topology.
questions.prompt_html: What do you mean by Network Topology? Explain Star, Ring and Bus Topology.
questions.solution_html:
Network Topology: Physical/logical interconnection geometry of network devices and links.

  • Star: All nodes connect individually to a central hub/switch. Easy fault isolation; single point of failure at hub.
  • Ring: Nodes form a closed unidirectional loop; tokens pass node-to-node. No collisions, but one broken link can halt the ring unless dual-ringed.
  • Bus: All nodes tap onto one shared backbone cable terminated at both ends. Economical cabling; backbone break disables entire bus and signals contend.

questions.prompt_text: State any three front panel controls of CRO and give use of each control.
questions.prompt_html: State any three front panel controls of CRO and give use of each control.
questions.solution_html:
1. VOLTS/DIV: Selects vertical amplifier sensitivity (vertical scale factor in V/div) to set waveform height on screen.
  2. TIME/DIV: Selects horizontal time-base sweep speed to control number of waveform cycles displayed horizontally.
  3. INTENSITY & FOCUS: Adjust beam brightness (control grid bias) and trace sharpness (focusing anode voltage). (Also Position X/Y, Trigger Level, AC-GND-DC coupling.)

questions.prompt_text: Explain with diagram and wave form working of R-C filter for reducing ripple.
questions.prompt_html: Explain with diagram and wave form working of R-C filter for reducing ripple.
questions.solution_html:
An RC π-filter adds a series resistor R between two shunt capacitors C1 and C2.

  • C1 removes most initial rectifier ripple by charging to Vm.
  • Series resistor R and shunt capacitor C2 form a low-pass voltage divider where XC2 « R at ripple frequency (100 Hz), shunting remaining AC ripple to ground while DC drops slightly across R.
  • Resulting output waveform across C2 is much smoother DC with low ripple.

questions.prompt_text: Explain the working of differentiator circuit using operational amplifier. Derive expression for output voltage.
questions.prompt_html: Explain the working of differentiator circuit using operational amplifier. Derive expression for output voltage.
questions.solution_html:
Circuit: Input Vin passes through capacitor C to the (−) terminal; resistor Rf feeds output back to (−); (+) is grounded.

Derivation:

  • Because (−) is at virtual ground (0 V), current through C is IC = C (dVin / dt).
  • Feedback current through Rf is If = −Vout / Rf.
  • Since IC = If ⇒ C (dVin/dt) = −Vout/Rf ⇒ Vout = −Rf C (dVin / dt).
  • Converts square waves into spikes / triangular waves into square waves.

questions.prompt_text: Draw basic circuit for Schmitt trigger using Op-Amp. and explain the terms: (i) UTP (ii) LTP (iii) Hysteresis
questions.prompt_html:
Draw basic circuit for Schmitt trigger using Op-Amp and explain the terms:

(i) UTP   (ii) LTP   (iii) Hysteresis
questions.solution_html:
Circuit: Vin goes to inverting (−) pin; voltage divider R1, R2 feeds positive feedback from Vout to (+) pin (β = R2/(R1+R2)).

  • (i) UTP (Upper Trigger Point): The positive input threshold voltage at which output switches from +Vsat to −Vsat: UTP = +βVsat.
  • (ii) LTP (Lower Trigger Point): The negative input threshold voltage at which output switches back from −Vsat to +Vsat: LTP = −βVsat.
  • (iii) Hysteresis (VH): Voltage dead-band gap between trigger thresholds: VH = UTP − LTP = 2βVsat, giving high noise immunity.

questions.prompt_text: Draw a block-diagram showing basic elements of a Fiber Optical Communication System. Explain function of each block in brief.
questions.prompt_html: Draw a block-diagram showing basic elements of a Fiber Optical Communication System. Explain function of each block in brief.
questions.solution_html:

  2. Optical Transmitter (LED / Laser Diode): Converts coded electrical signal into modulated light pulses.
  3. Optical Fiber Cable: Core-cladding glass/plastic guide that carries light over long distances via Total Internal Reflection.

questions.prompt_text: Explain electro-static focussing system of a CRT (Cathode Ray Tube).
questions.prompt_html: Explain electro-static focussing system of a CRT (Cathode Ray Tube).
questions.solution_html:
Consists of three cylindrical coaxial anodes inside the CRT neck: Pre-accelerating anode (A1) and Accelerating anode (A3) held at high fixed +ve voltage (e.g. +1500 V), flanking a central Focusing anode (A2) at lower variable +ve voltage (~300–500 V).

  • Voltage difference creates curved equipotential electric-field surfaces between A1-A2 and A2-A3 acting as an electron lens.
  • Diverging off-axis electrons are deflected toward the axis twice and converge cleanly to a sharp point right on the phosphor screen by tuning A2.

questions.prompt_text: Explain the use of CRO for measurement of phase.
questions.prompt_html: Explain the use of CRO for measurement of phase.
questions.solution_html:
Lissajous Figure (X-Y Mode) Method:

  • Switch time-base to X-Y (external horizontal) mode. Apply two same-frequency sine waves Vx and Vy to X and Y inputs with equal screen amplitudes.
  • Measure the vertical intercept Y1 (where X = 0) and maximum positive vertical height Y2 of the resulting ellipse.
  • Phase difference φ = sin−1(Y1 / Y2). (0°: straight line +slope; 90°: circle; 180°: line −slope).

questions.prompt_text: In Full Wave Rectifier, if primary of transformer is connected to 230V, 50 Hz and secondary voltage is 12-0-12V. Calculate: (i) Output DC voltage (ii) PIV of the diode (iii) Output ripple frequency
questions.prompt_html:
In Full Wave Rectifier, if primary of transformer is connected to 230V, 50 Hz and secondary voltage is 12-0-12V. Calculate:

(i) Output DC voltage   (ii) PIV of the diode   (iii) Output ripple frequency
questions.solution_html:
Given: Secondary voltage across each half Vrms = 12 V, fin = 50 Hz.

  • Peak voltage per half-winding: Vm = 12 × √2 = 16.97 V
  • (i) Output DC voltage: Vdc = 2Vm / π = (2 × 16.97) / 3.1416 = 10.80 V
  • (ii) PIV of each diode (centre-tapped FWR): PIV = 2Vm = 2 × 16.97 = 33.94 V
  • (iii) Output ripple frequency: fripple = 2 fin = 2 × 50 = 100 Hz

questions.prompt_text: Explain how Op-amplifier is used as a Buffer. Draw suitable circuit diagram.
questions.prompt_html: Explain how Op-amplifier is used as a Buffer. Draw suitable circuit diagram.
questions.solution_html:
Voltage Follower (Unity-Gain Buffer): Direct wire feedback connects Vout to (−) (so Rf = 0, R1 = ∞), and Vin connects to (+).

  • By virtual short, V− = V+ = Vin; since Vout = V−, Vout = Vin (Gain Av = +1, zero phase shift).
  • Offers extremely high input impedance (~MΩ/GΩ) and near-zero output impedance (~Ω), preventing source loading when driving low-impedance stages.

questions.prompt_text: Give any three advantages of FM over AM.
questions.prompt_html: Give any three advantages of FM over AM.
questions.solution_html:
1. Superior Noise Immunity: Atmospheric noise alters signal amplitude, which FM limiters clip cleanly while preserving frequency information.
  2. Higher Transmitted Efficiency: All transmitted power stays useful regardless of modulation depth; amplitude remains constant.
  3. Better Audio Fidelity & Guard Bands: Wider audio bandwidth (~15 kHz) gives Hi-Fi sound, and FM allows capture effect/less adjacent-channel interference.

questions.prompt_text: Explain how IC 555 can be used as a Pulse Position Modulator (PPM).
questions.prompt_html: Explain how IC 555 can be used as a Pulse Position Modulator (PPM).
questions.solution_html:
• IC 555 is configured as a monostable multivibrator with negative clock/trigger pulses applied continuously to Pin 2 (Trigger).
  • The modulating analog signal Vmod is applied to Pin 5 (Control Voltage).
  • Vmod shifts the upper comparator reference level (normally 2/3 VCC), varying the capacitor charge time and thus shifting the falling edge / trailing pulse position in proportion to Vmod. (Feeding PWM edge to a second fixed monostable outputs constant-width PPM pulses.)

questions.prompt_text: State Active Transducers. Explain Optocoupler.
questions.prompt_html: State Active Transducers. Explain Optocoupler.
questions.solution_html:
Active Transducers: Self-generating transducers that convert physical energy directly into electrical output without external power (e.g., Piezoelectric crystal, Thermocouple, Solar/Photovoltaic cell, Moving-coil microphone).

Optocoupler (Opto-isolator): Combines an IR LED (input transmitter) and a phototransistor/photodiode inside a light-tight DIP IC package (e.g., MCT2E).

  • Input electrical current lights the LED proportional to signal; light couples across the insulating gap to trigger the phototransistor output.
  • Provides complete galvanic electrical isolation (kV-range) between low-voltage logic circuits and noisy/high-voltage AC loads.

questions.prompt_text: Explain any four characteristics of a Power Supply.
questions.prompt_html: Explain any four characteristics of a Power Supply.
questions.solution_html:
1. Load Regulation: Ability to keep DC output constant when load current changes from no-load to full-load: %LR = [(VNL − VFL)/VFL] × 100%.
  2. Line (Source) Regulation: Ability to maintain steady output despite AC mains input voltage fluctuations: %Reg = (ΔVout / ΔVin) × 100%.
  3. Output Impedance (Rout): Ratio ΔVout / ΔIL; ideally 0 Ω so voltage doesn't sag under heavy current.
  4. Ripple Factor / Ripple Rejection & Over-current Protection: Low residual AC ripple on output DC plus current-limiting / thermal shutdown safety.

questions.prompt_text: How Op-amplifier can be used as a Subtractor?
questions.prompt_html: How Op-amplifier can be used as a Subtractor?
questions.solution_html:
Uses a differential amplifier configuration with both inverting and non-inverting inputs:

  • V1 connects via R1 to (−) with feedback resistor Rf.
  • V2 connects via R2 to (+) with resistor R3 from (+) to ground.
  • By superposition:
    With V2=0: Vo1 = −(Rf/R1)V1.
    With V1=0: V+ = [R3/(R2+R3)]V2, so Vo2 = (1 + Rf/R1)V+.
  • If R1 = R2 = R3 = Rf = R: Vo1 = −V1 and Vo2 = +V2 ⇒ Vout = V2 − V1.

questions.prompt_text: Draw general block-diagram of a pulsed radar and explain function of each block in brief.

questions.prompt_text: What is Amplitude Modulation? Draw Waveforms. Explain importance of sidebands in Amplitude Modulation.
questions.prompt_html: What is Amplitude Modulation? Draw Waveforms. Explain importance of sidebands in Amplitude Modulation.

questions.prompt_text: Draw frequency response curve of an Operational Amplifier and explain.
questions.prompt_html: Draw frequency response curve of an Operational Amplifier and explain.

questions.prompt_text: Explain the working of voltage regulator using series pass transistor.
questions.prompt_html: Explain the working of voltage regulator using series pass transistor.
questions.solution_html:
An NPN transistor is connected in series with the load (collector to Vin, emitter to Vout); its base connects to a Zener reference VZ powered through resistor R.

  • Output Voltage: Vout = VZ − VBE (constant, ~VZ − 0.7 V).
  • Regulation Action: Because high load current flows through collector-emitter, only small base current IB = IL/β loads the Zener. If Vout tries to drop, VBE = VZ − Vout increases → transistor conducts harder → restores Vout. Power dissipated in pass transistor PD = (Vin − Vout)IL.

questions.prompt_text: Explain with circuit diagram the working of Op-Amp as a Schmitt Trigger. Draw transfer characteristics.
questions.prompt_html: Explain with circuit diagram the working of Op-Amp as a Schmitt Trigger. Draw transfer characteristics.
questions.solution_html:
Positive feedback divider R1, R2 sends fraction βVout (β = R2/(R1+R2)) to (+); Vin goes to (−).

  • When Vout = +Vsat, (+) pin sits at UTP = +βVsat. As Vin rises above UTP, output regeneratively snaps to −Vsat.
  • Reference now drops to LTP = −βVsat. Output switches back to +Vsat only when Vin falls below LTP.
  • Transfer characteristic (Vout vs Vin) forms a rectangular hysteresis loop between LTP and UTP.

  • Very high sensitivity and negligible loading force, suitable for tiny displacements.

questions.prompt_text: Define the following terms in frequency modulation: (i) Frequency deviation (ii) Carrier swing (iii) Modulation Index
questions.prompt_html:
Define the following terms in frequency modulation:

(i) Frequency deviation   (ii) Carrier swing   (iii) Modulation Index

  • (ii) Carrier Swing (CS): Total peak-to-peak variation in carrier frequency from minimum to maximum: CS = 2 × Δf.
  • (iii) Modulation Index (mf): Ratio of maximum frequency deviation to modulating signal frequency: mf = Δf / fm.

questions.prompt_text: For IC-555 timer, connected in Astable Mode, calculate: (i) Charging time (ii) Discharging time (iii) Output frequency. Given Ra = 10 kOhm, Rb = 12 kOhm, C = 0.1 uF

questions.prompt_text: Draw and explain the circuit diagram of voltage regulator using Zener diode. Explain load regulation and line regulation.
questions.prompt_html: Draw and explain the circuit diagram of voltage regulator using Zener diode. Explain load regulation and line regulation.
questions.solution_html:

questions.prompt_text: Explain Non Inverting Op-Amp using circuit diagram. Derive expression for its gain. Calculate the gain if Rf = 5 kOhm, Ri = 1 kOhm
questions.prompt_html: Explain Non Inverting Op-Amp using circuit diagram. Derive expression for its gain. Calculate the gain if Rf = 5 kΩ, Ri = 1 kΩ.
questions.solution_html:
Circuit: Input Vin applies directly to (+); potential divider Rf, Ri connects output to (−) and ground.

Derivation:

  • By virtual short, V− = V+ = Vin.
  • Zero op-amp input current ⇒ V− = Vout [Ri / (Ri + Rf)].
  • Therefore Vout / Vin = 1 + (Rf / Ri) (zero phase shift).

Calculation: Av = 1 + (5 / 1) = 6.

  • When CLK = 1: Master latches J-K input state while Slave is isolated (holds previous output).
  • When CLK → 0 (falling edge): Master locks out new inputs while Slave copies Master's state to Q, Q̅.
  • Completely eliminates the race-around condition when J = K = 1.

questions.prompt_text: Draw and explain basic circuit of TTL NOR gate.

questions.solution_html:
A 2-input TTL NOR gate uses two parallel input phase-splitter stages (Q1A-Q2A and Q1B-Q2B with collectors/emitters tied together) driving a totem-pole output stage (Q3-Q4) and pull-down transistor.

  • If any input (A or B) is HIGH, its transistor Q2 saturates, pulling output transistor Q4 ON → Y = LOW (0).

questions.solution_html:

  2. While Vin > Vdac, comparator stays HIGH, enabling AND gate so clock pulses increment the counter and Vdac steps up in a staircase ramp.
  3. The instant Vdac ≥ Vin, comparator goes LOW, locking the AND gate. Counter holds the digital equivalent of Vin.

questions.prompt_text: What is Parallel Counter (Synchronous)? Write its two advantages.
questions.prompt_html: What is Parallel Counter (Synchronous)? Write its two advantages.
questions.solution_html:
Counter in which every flip-flop receives the master clock pulse simultaneously instead of rippling stage-by-stage.

Two Advantages: (1) High operating speed with no cumulative propagation delay; (2) Glitch-free synchronous state transitions for high-speed decoding.

questions.solution_html: Asynchronous override inputs (PR forces Q=1; CLR forces Q=0) active-LOW independent of clock, used to initialize flip-flops/counters or truncate MOD cycles.

questions.prompt_text: Explain the working of Successive approximation A/D converter.
questions.prompt_html: Explain the working of Successive approximation A/D converter.
questions.solution_html:
Uses a Successive Approximation Register (SAR), DAC, and comparator to perform a binary search bit-by-bit from MSB down to LSB:

  1. Sets MSB = 1 first (half scale); if DAC output Vdac > Vin, resets MSB to 0, else keeps 1.
  2. Repeats sequentially for each lower bit down to LSB.
  3. Always finishes an n-bit conversion in exactly n clock cycles, regardless of Vin amplitude.

questions.prompt_text: What do you mean by: (i) LSB (ii) MSB (iii) Nibble (iv) Byte
questions.prompt_html:
What do you mean by:
(i) LSB   (ii) MSB   (iii) Nibble   (iv) Byte
questions.solution_html:
• (i) LSB (Least Significant Bit): Rightmost bit in a binary number carrying smallest positional weight (20 = 1).
  • (ii) MSB (Most Significant Bit): Leftmost bit carrying largest positional weight (2n−1).
  • (iii) Nibble: Group of 4 bits (represents 1 hexadecimal digit).
  • (iv) Byte: Group of 8 bits (standard unit of computer memory capacity).

questions.prompt_text: Prove the following identities using boolean laws: (i) ABC + A.overline(B)C + AB.overline(C) = A(B + C)  (ii) (A + B)(A + C) = A + BC
questions.prompt_html:
Prove the following identities using Boolean laws:
(i) ABC + ABC + ABC = A(B + C)
(ii) (A + B)(A + C) = A + BC
questions.solution_html:
1. (i) LHS = AC(B + B) + ABC = AC(1) + ABC = A(C + BC) = A(C + B) [via C + BC = C + B] = A(B + C) = RHS
  2. (ii) LHS = A·A + AC + AB + BC = A + AC + AB + BC = A(1 + C + B) + BC = A + BC = RHS

questions.prompt_text: What is Multiplexer? Obtain 8:1 multiplexer using two 4:1 multiplexer.
questions.prompt_html: What is Multiplexer? Obtain 8:1 multiplexer using two 4:1 multiplexer.
questions.solution_html:
Multiplexer: Many-to-one data selector routing 1 of 2n inputs to a single output under n select lines.

8:1 using two 4:1 MUXes: Share B, C as common S1, S0 on both ICs; route A and A to opposite Enable strobes and OR their outputs.

questions.prompt_text: Explain the working of Weighted Resistor DAC? State its drawbacks.
questions.prompt_html: Explain the working of Weighted Resistor DAC. State its drawbacks.
questions.solution_html: Uses binary-weighted resistors (R, 2R, 4R, 8R) switched between Vref and 0 V into an op-amp summing junction. Drawbacks: Large resistance spread (2n−1R for n bits) makes matched precision resistor fabrication on ICs impractical for high resolution.
